rules.sentence: Sepsis and its associated hemodynamic instability increase susceptibility to ventricular fibrillation.
Use of stimulants such as cocaine and methamphetamines is another significant trigger.
Electrolyte disturbances, particularly hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, are strongly associated with ventricular fibrillation.[4]
QT-prolonging medications may also precipitate the arrhythmia.
Channelopathies, including long QT syndrome, short QT syndrome, and Brugada syndrome, are well-established causes of ventricular fibrillation.

Congenital and structural heart diseases such as tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and mitral valve prolapse are also linked to ventricular arrhythmogenesis and ventricular fibrillation.[5]
Ventricular fibrillation often represents the terminal rhythm following prolonged ventricular tachycardia and cardiac arrest.[6]
